subject: history
title: Five-Year Plans, Terror and Barbarossa
welcome_lead: Industry, terror and the Nazi-Soviet collision.
meta_desc: -Level adventure on the Five-Year Plans, Great Terror 1936-38, Nazi-Soviet Pact 1939 and Operation Barbarossa June 1941.
final_note: You can analyse how Stalinist transformation prepared Russia for total war.

concepts.def: Centrally directed industrial plans from October 1928 prioritising heavy industry, steel and coal.
1929-33 forced amalgamation of peasant farms into kolkhozes; dekulakisation displaced and killed millions.
Ukrainian famine resulting from grain procurement and policy; approximately 3.5-5 million Ukrainian deaths.
Mass purges including the Moscow Show Trials, Yezhovshchina and Order 00447; an estimated 700,000 executions.
Non-aggression treaty signed 23 August 1939 (Molotov-Ribbentrop), with secret protocol partitioning Eastern Europe.
Nazi invasion of the USSR launched 22 June 1941 with 3.5 million Axis troops along an 1,800-mile front.

walkthroughs.body_html: The First Five-Year Plan (1928-32) targeted heavy industry; steel output rose from 4 to 17 million tonnes by 1937. Collectivisation forced peasants into kolkhozes; dekulakisation displaced ~5 million. The Holodomor (1932-33) devastated Ukraine. Magnitogorsk and Dneprostroi exemplified industrial gigantism. The Stakhanovite movement (1935) drove productivity.

Kirov's murder (1 December 1934) initiated the spiral. The Moscow Show Trials (1936-38) destroyed Zinoviev, Kamenev, Bukharin and others. Order 00447 (July 1937) targeted 'former kulaks, criminals and other anti-Soviet elements'. The Red Army purge (1937-38) killed three of five marshals. Gulag population rose to about 1.8 million by 1938.

The Nazi-Soviet Pact (August 1939) divided Poland (September 1939); Soviet annexations followed of the Baltic states, Bessarabia and parts of Romania (1940). The Winter War with Finland (November 1939-March 1940) exposed Red Army weakness. On 22 June 1941 Operation Barbarossa began; Kiev, Minsk and Smolensk fell, the Wehrmacht reached Moscow's outskirts before being halted in December 1941.

A joint declaration of war on Britain
Soviet membership of the Axis
Exchange of Polish and German citizens

mcqs.q: How successful were Stalin's Five Year Plans?
options: The Five Year Plans were Lenin's last great achievement.
Heavy industry and steel output grew dramatically; consumer goods, quality and worker conditions lagged badly; statistics were inflated, but the USSR became an industrial power.
The Five Year Plans turned the USSR into the most prosperous country in the world.
The Terror was a response to a planned coup by Trotsky.

mcqs.q: Why did Stalin launch the Great Terror?
options: The Five Year Plans were Lenin's last great achievement.
Stalin was simply mentally ill and killed people at random.
The Terror was a response to a planned coup by Trotsky.
A combination of genuine paranoia, removal of political rivals, consolidation of personal power, and the dynamics of a self-reinforcing security apparatus.
It failed to overthrow the Tsar but forced the October Manifesto creating the Duma, exposing autocracy's weaknesses and rehearsing the structures of 1917.
The Five Year Plans were Lenin's last great achievement.
The 1905 Revolution achieved nothing because the Tsar stayed in power.
The 1905 Revolution was led by Lenin from the Winter Palace.
